paper_id: Li et al. - 2008 - Arnetminer expertise oriented search using social networks
title: Arnetminer: expertise oriented search using social networks
motivation: Funding agencies and researchers need to find experts, detect conflicts of interest, assign reviewers, but data is distributed and unstructured
problem_framing: Expertise oriented search as ranking persons by topic relevance in a co-authorship social network with propagation
key_insight: Relevance propagates through co-authorship edges; social network structure + individual profiles outperform local-only methods
method_signature: Relevance propagation expert finding with two-stage heap-Dijkstra association search
evaluation_criteria: P@K, MAP, bpref for expert finding; runtime seconds for association search
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Name disambiguation only uses heuristic rules; cannot handle cases outside rule patterns
evidence_for_taste: relevance of a researcher is propagated
over a hundred times faster than the baseline
our methods can achieve high performances
our approach can achieve a high accuracy
thinking_moves: Convert expert finding into topic relevance calculation with propagation through network edges
Use heap-Dijkstra to precompute shortest paths, then enumerate near-shortest paths for efficiency
Combine local profile information with network structure via weighted co-authorship edges
Ground truth as committee membership of top conferences
